title: A home-screen widget Start whose routine could not be read drops the member on the Workout tab with no message
what: When the widget's Start link opens the app and the routine cannot be read at that moment, the app treats the routine as deleted and quietly shows the Workout tab. The member tapped Start and nothing starts, and nothing says why. The app's own rule says a failed widget start must be said, never a silent Workout tab.
expected: A routine that could not be read is told apart from a deleted one, and the member sees 'Couldn't start' with Try again.
how_often: rarely, when the phone's storage is slow or busy
fix_line: Treat a failed routine read as a failed start and show the Couldn't start message

title: Failed saves on several screens show 'try again' but leave no record of what went wrong
what: When finishing a workout, saving changes to a past workout, saving a built plan, adding a ready program, swapping an exercise in a routine, or deleting, saving or re-dating a progress photo fails, the member sees a calm 'Could not save, try again' message, but the error itself is thrown away. If it keeps failing for a member, nobody can find out why from the phone's log or a feedback report.
expected: Every failure that shows a try-again message also writes the error to the log.
how_often: every failed save on these screens
fix_line: Log the error next to each try-again message

title: Stats tells a member to add body weight or do a bench press when it simply could not read their numbers
what: On the Statistics page, if reading the latest body weight fails, the strength score box says 'Add your body weight' even when the member has logged it. If reading the lift history fails, it says 'No score yet, do a bench press, squat or deadlift' to a member who has done many. Both failures are hidden, so the page shows wrong advice instead of saying it could not load.
expected: A failed read shows 'Couldn't load' with Try again, and the add-weight or no-score advice shows only when the data is really missing.
fix_line: Keep the failure and show a load error in the strength box instead of the empty advice

title: The switched-off Muscles ready today and Quick workout pages are still kept in the app
what: The card that opened these two pages was switched off on 5 Nov and no screen shows it any more, but the two pages, the card and their loaders (about 750 lines) are still in the app and still kept up to date by hand. Only the quick-workout rules have a test; the pages have none.
expected: Either the pages are removed, or they are kept behind a clear switch with a test that they stay off.
how_often: every change near the Workout tab
fix_line: Remove the switched-off pages and card, or put them behind a tested switch

title: A timed hold is written by two different rules: '1 min 30 s' in the routine preview, '90 s' in the Hevy import check
what: The routine preview and the Hevy routine import steps each write their own wording for a timed set. A 90-second hold reads '1 min 30 s' on one and '90 s' on the other, so the same routine looks different before and after it is brought in.
expected: One shared rule writes hold times everywhere.
how_often: every timed hold not a whole minute
fix_line: Use one shared hold-time wording on both screens

title: The quick tests of the live workout screen only look for words in its code; no quick test opens any of these screens
what: Tests that promise 'Save changes writes the ticked sets and says what it leaves out' and 'the workout screen scrolls back to the first unticked exercise' pass when a line of code is present, whatever the screen really does. None of the 56 screens in this area is opened by any quick test; only the slower cloud phone runs drive them.
expected: Key live-workout behaviours are checked by running them, not by matching words in the code.
how_often: every change to the live workout screen
fix_line: Turn the word checks into tests that run the save and resume steps
